messages.text: hi sarah i am interested to make the deign for bit mining machine by using bm1373 chip using can you help me in any technical information about bm1373
Handed to the team · Chip-level design specs for the BM1373 aren't in our product data

Happy to point you in the right direction. What I can tell you from our side: our Magic Miner 40T runs the BM1370, 30 chips of it. A BM1373 build costs roughly double, which is why we didn't go that route. I don't have the chip-level spec sheet in front of me, so I've put your question to JD, who handles our hardware.

He picks it up today at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email. What's your email address, and what hashrate are you aiming for?
yes my mail is (email hidden) and i want to build device which achieve 100TH/s

Got it, I've added (email hidden) to the question for JD.

For scale: 100 TH/s at current chip efficiency is roughly 2 kW, so you're designing around a dedicated 240V circuit, real airflow and a serious PSU. Our closest box is the PunkHash 70T, 70 TH/s at about 1.45 kW, $1,100, though it's not buyable right now.

JD picks this up today at 10am ET and replies to your email. Is this a one-off build or something you want to produce?
yes i will handle real airflow and PSU

Good. Then the hard parts left are the chip supply and the control board: Bitmain doesn't sell BM1373 dies to individuals, so most people building at that scale source hashboards rather than bare chips. That's exactly what JD can talk you through.

He has your question and your email, and picks it up today at 10am ET.

One thing that helps him answer: is this for home use, or are you planning to sell the units?
currently I want to design it's for my own interest because I am also a hardware design engineer. for just testing purpose and make research on thermal control

That's useful context, I've added it. A thermal research build changes the answer a lot, since you care about J/TH under load and hashboard temperature behaviour, not just raw hashrate.

For reference, our PunkHash 70T runs about 21 J/TH at 1.45 kW, and the Magic Miner 40T uses 30 BM1370 chips, so that's a real data point on chip count versus hashrate.

JD has all of this and emails you today after 10am ET. Anything else while you're here?

I thinks for now it's fine. waiting JDs response.
thanks for your time

Any time. JD will come back to you at that address today.

Before you go, one thing: what made you land on the BM1373 specifically rather than a chip you can actually buy in small quantities?
Because BM1373 is higher efficient and low in thermal

That makes sense.

Where did you get the efficiency and thermal figures for it? Knowing the source helps JD point you at the right numbers.
Understood, thanks for telling me. JD will sanity-check those numbers for you when he writes today after 10am ET.
I didn't receive any mail please concern with JDs

Sorry about that, I've put it back in front of JD with your email on it, (email hidden)

He's offline right now and picks it up today from 10am ET, and the answer comes to that address. Worth checking your spam folder too, since our mail can land there.

context.pop: Hey, it's Sarah from HeliumDeploy. Looking for a home Bitcoin miner? Happy to help you pick one.
